(a) Extension.—Notwithstanding section 2002 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (division B of Public Law 112–239; 126 Stat. 2118), the authorizations set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2201 of that Act (126 Stat. 2122) and extended by section 2206 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (division B of Public Law 114–92; 129 Stat. 1151), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2017, or the date of the enactment of an Act authorizing funds for military construction for fiscal year 2018, whichever is later. 
    (b) Table.—The table referred to in subsection (a) is as follows:

fable.w: This section only extends the expiration date of earlier Navy military construction project authorizations and lists the projects and amounts. The tempting reading is that naming state and foreign locations (California, South Carolina, Greece) implies coordination with outside governments, but these are just project sites. No outside party is consulted, heard, given a comment opportunity, or granted a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: the authorizations set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2201 of that Act (126 Stat. 2122) and extended by section 2206 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (division B of Public Law 114–92; 129 Stat. 1151), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2017

qwen_block.w: This section extends the authorization of appropriations for specific military construction projects. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public) in the decision-making process. The text merely lists locations and amounts for federal spending.
qwen_block.s: the authorizations set forth in the table in subsection (b)... shall remain in effect until October 1, 2017

opus.w: The section only extends fiscal year 2013 Navy military construction project authorizations until October 1, 2017, or until the fiscal year 2018 authorization act is enacted, whichever is later. It lists the projects and their amounts. It has no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue that involves anyone outside the federal government. Naming specific installations and earlier Acts does not bring any outside party into a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely extends the authorization of appropriations for specific military construction projects. It lists locations and amounts but does not require any consultation, coordination, or participation with state, local, tribal, or private entities. The decision-making process described is internal to the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: The table referred to in subsection (a) is as follows: Navy: Extension of 2013 Project Authorizations
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the projects are located in various states and countries (e.g., Greece, California), there is an implicit requirement for coordination with local or foreign entities. However, the text itself only lists authorizations for funds and project locations; it does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or participation process with outside parties. The decision-making authority rests entirely with the federal government (specifically the Department of Defense/Navy).
